name: The four-letter verb (rubāʿī)
definition: A verb with four root letters, such as daḥraja, 'he rolled'; bare on the pattern faʿlala, with its own augmented patterns.
body: The bare rubāʿī has one pattern, faʿlala (daḥraja, yudaḥriju); its augmented forms are tafaʿlala (tadaḥraja, compliant), ifʿanlala and ifʿalalla (iqshaʿarra, 'to shudder'). Some three-letter verbs are built to match it by an added letter: these are the mulḥaq verbs.

examples.text: daḥraja, yudaḥriju: the bare four-letter verb.
